questions.question: Two parallel plates are $d = 5\ \mathrm{mm} = 5\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m}$ apart and maintain a potential difference of $V = 100\ \mathrm{V}$. Find the electric field between the plates.
questions.answer:
In a uniform field between parallel plates:

$E = \dfrac{V}{d} = \dfrac{100}{5\times10^{-3}} = 2\times10^4\ \mathrm{V/m} = 20{,}000\ \mathrm{N/C}$

The field is directed from the positive plate to the negative plate.

questions.question: A proton ($m = 1.67\times10^{-27}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $q = 1.6\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$) is released from rest between two charged plates ($E = 5\times10^4\ \mathrm{N/C}$, plate separation $d = 0.02\ \mathrm{m}$). Find: (a) the acceleration, (b) the speed when it reaches the negative plate.

An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of $V = 200\ \mathrm{V}$. Find: (a) the kinetic energy gained, (b) the final speed. ($m_e = 9.11\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$)
In a uniform electric field $E = 3000\ \mathrm{N/C}$, find the work done by the field to move a charge $q = 2\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ a distance $d = 0.05\ \mathrm{m}$ parallel to the field.
questions.answer:
$W = qEd = 2\times10^{-6} \times 3000 \times 0.05 = 3\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J} = 0.3\ \mathrm{mJ}$

If the charge moves perpendicular to the field: $W = qEd\cos(90°) = 0$.

Work by the electric field = $q\Delta V$ where $\Delta V = -Ed$ (potential drops in the direction of $E$).

questions.question: The electric potential at a distance $r$ from a point charge $q$ is $V = kq/r$. Two points A and B are at distances $r_A = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ and $r_B = 0.3\ \mathrm{m}$ from a $q = 5\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ charge. Find the potential difference $V_A - V_B$ and the work done to move a $2\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ charge from B to A.
questions.answer:
$V_A = k\dfrac{q}{r_A} = 9\times10^9 \times \dfrac{5\times10^{-6}}{0.1} = 4.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{V}$

$V_B = k\dfrac{q}{r_B} = 9\times10^9 \times \dfrac{5\times10^{-6}}{0.3} = 1.5\times10^5\ \mathrm{V}$

$V_A - V_B = 3.0\times10^5\ \mathrm{V}$

Work done by the field to move $q_0 = 2\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ from B to A:

$W = q_0(V_B - V_A) = 2\times10^{-6} \times (-3.0\times10^5) = -0.6\ \mathrm{J}$

(Negative: moving a positive charge to higher potential requires external work.)

questions.question: An electron enters parallel plates horizontally at speed $v_0 = 2\times10^7\ \mathrm{m/s}$. The plates are $L = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ long and have $E = 4\times10^4\ \mathrm{N/C}$ (vertical). Find the vertical deflection as the electron exits the plates.
questions.answer:
Time in the field: $t = L/v_0 = 0.1/(2\times10^7) = 5\times10^{-9}\ \mathrm{s}$

Vertical acceleration: $a = eE/m_e = 1.6\times10^{-19} \times 4\times10^4 / 9.11\times10^{-31}$

$= 6.4\times10^{-15}/9.11\times10^{-31} = 7.03\times10^{15}\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$

Vertical deflection:

$y = \frac{1}{2}at^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 7.03\times10^{15} \times (5\times10^{-9})^2$

$= \frac{1}{2} \times 7.03\times10^{15} \times 2.5\times10^{-17} = 0.0879\ \mathrm{m} \approx 8.8\ \mathrm{cm}$

questions.question: A uniform electric field of $E = 500\ \mathrm{V/m}$ points in the $+x$ direction. Find the potential difference $V_A - V_B$ between points A$(x=0)$ and B$(x=0.4\ \mathrm{m})$.
questions.answer:
In a uniform field, the potential decreases in the direction of the field:

$V_A - V_B = E \times d_{AB} = 500 \times 0.4 = 200\ \mathrm{V}$

Point A is at higher potential than B (electric field points from high to low potential).

General formula: $V_A - V_B = E \cdot (x_B - x_A)$ for field in $+x$ direction.

questions.question: Show that the relationship between electric field $E$ and potential $V$ in a uniform field is $E = -dV/dx$. Verify with a field of $E = 200\ \mathrm{V/m}$ and $V(0) = 1000\ \mathrm{V}$.
questions.answer:
The work done by the field on charge $q$ moving $dx$ in the $+x$ direction:

$dW = qE\,dx$

By the relation between work and potential: $dW = -q\,dV$ (potential energy decreases)

$qE\,dx = -q\,dV$

$$E = -\dfrac{dV}{dx}$$

For uniform $E = 200\ \mathrm{V/m}$: $V(x) = V(0) - E \cdot x = 1000 - 200x$

Check: $-dV/dx = -(-200) = 200\ \mathrm{V/m}$ ✓

At $x = 2\ \mathrm{m}$: $V = 1000 - 400 = 600\ \mathrm{V}$

questions.question: A charge $q = -3\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ is held in a uniform electric field. The potential at its location is $V = 400\ \mathrm{V}$. Find: (a) the electric potential energy of the charge, (b) the work done by an external force to move it to a point where $V' = 100\ \mathrm{V}$.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $U = qV = (-3\times10^{-6}) \times 400 = -1.2\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{J} = -1.2\ \mathrm{mJ}$

**(b)** Work done by external force (against field):

$W_{\text{ext}} = \Delta U = q(V' - V) = (-3\times10^{-6})(100 - 400) = (-3\times10^{-6})(-300) = 9\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{J} = 0.9\ \mathrm{mJ}$

(Positive work must be done by the external force to move the negative charge to lower potential.)

questions.question: Two parallel plates are separated by $d = 0.01\ \mathrm{m}$ and connected to a battery of $\mathcal{E} = 12\ \mathrm{V}$. An oil droplet of mass $m = 5\times10^{-15}\ \mathrm{kg}$ and charge $q$ is suspended motionless between the plates. Find $q$ and the number of excess electrons. ($g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$)
questions.answer:
Equilibrium: electric force = gravity

$qE = mg$

$E = V/d = 12/0.01 = 1200\ \mathrm{V/m}$

$q = \dfrac{mg}{E} = \dfrac{5\times10^{-15} \times 10}{1200} = \dfrac{5\times10^{-14}}{1200} = 4.17\times10^{-17}\ \mathrm{C}$

Number of excess electrons: $n = q/e = 4.17\times10^{-17}/1.6\times10^{-19} \approx 260$

(Millikan oil-drop experiment setup)
